method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (the text's no where it says no; NOTHING, with a NOTHING-kind tag, where it does not answer); the dates in one module, the rules and exported questions in another, the cases in a third; one regulative rule (commencing within the time the governing place's limitation law allows, made part of the law applied by s 5) run by EVALTRACE inside an exported question that takes only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Choice of Law (Limitation Periods) Act 1994 (NT), Act No. 45 of 1994, reprint REPC071 as in force at 7 November 1994 (no amendment listed), current on the NT Legislation register on 6 November 2026, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/Choice-of-Law-Limitation-Periods-Act-1994-NT-current-reprint-REPC071.txt

seat: the person bringing a claim: the claimant whose claim is before a court of the Northern Territory or an arbitrator and is governed by the law of an Australian State, another Territory or New Zealand (clpnt-claims.l4)

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run clpnt-dates.l4 ; l4 run clpnt-claims.l4 ; l4 run clpnt-cases.l4
checks.result: 55 assertions written, 55 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07); a deliberately wrong assertion in a scratch copy showed as failed
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the text.

scope: The whole operative Act, from the claimant's seat. In: s 3 (application), s 4 (court, limitation law), s 5 (characterisation of limitation laws), s 6 (exercise of discretion under limitation law); the commencement date under s 2. Out: s 1, s 2 (machinery); the limitation laws of the other places and the NT Limitation Act 1981 (their last day asked as a fact). Reasons in NOTES.md.
also_reads: subjects/au/nt/limitation-act-1981 (the Territory's own limitation law, where Territory law governs)
